structure: Part 4 of repo:plantsfrontend: the commodity section of the high-risk plants linear journey, read in full. Paths below are under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/. (1) journeys/linear/features/commodity-type/: page.js, controller.js, template.njk, evaluation.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and commodity-type.fit.spec.js (15 tests), which cover the commodity type page, the journey's entry question at /notifications/{journeyId}/commodity-type. The *.test.js unit tests were left out, as the partition says. (2) journeys/linear/features/commodities/: page.js (two pages, the list 'commodities' and the entry sub-page 'commodities/details'), links.js (hrefs that carry index, removed and change=1), entry-index.js (index guarding), fields.js (answer names), line-form.js (per-field widgets, widths, limits and validation rules), evaluation.js (obligation bindings), list/list.controller.js and list.njk (the list page: table, change and remove, removal banner, the at-least-one floor), details/details.controller.js and details.njk (the category-first entry page that reveals per-category fields), copy/copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (one bundle for both pages), and fit/list.fit.spec.js (12 tests), fit/details.fit.spec.js (17 tests) and fit/axe.js (shared axe helper). (3) services/commodities/index.js: the set-owned, hard-coded commodity vocabulary (3 types, 9 categories, 15 genera, category-to-field map, origin constraints). (4) obligations/sections/commodity.js: the commodityType, commodityLines (floor of one), category and quantity obligations, and 7 per-line fields gated on category. I looked up two constants outside the slice so the hints could be stated in full: timing-windows.js (2 days and 4 days). I also looked up the shared save-action labels (shared/copy.en.js) and the caption 'About the consignment' (flow/section-captions). Claims run in this order: the commodity type page, then the list page, then the details page, then the service data, then the obligations. Every fit test is cited in the ref of at least one claim.

claims.statement: Changing the commodity type removes every saved commodity line whose category does not belong to the new type. Because categories partition by type, a real change of type removes every line.
When lines are kept after the commodity type is saved again, they are matched by category, genus and potato variety, not by position, so a kept line keeps the rest of its answers.

// Lines are reconciled by what identifies one to a trader, not by position: a
// line they can still see keeps the rest of its answers.

claims.statement: When a commodity type change removed lines, the page goes to the commodities list with ?removed=<count>, whichever save control was pressed, so the trader sees what was removed before moving on.
If saving the commodity type fails, the page re-renders with the shared recoverable-error state and HTTP status 500.

claims.statement: The commodity data (types, categories, genera and which fields each category asks) is a hard-coded vocabulary held in the plants frontend. It is not fetched from MDM, reference data or any other service.
claims.quote:
The set-owned commodity vocabulary.
 *
 * The service holds values, never the words a page shows for them: a label or
 * a hint is a copy leaf in the feature that renders it.
claims.note: Inferred because the module holds only frozen literal arrays and does no IO, which the obligation file confirms: 'an obligation module does no IO and reads no reference data'.

claims.statement: The plants commodity pages have no commodity catalogue search. Categories are radios filtered by commodity type, the genus is a type-ahead over a fixed list of 15, and species, commodity code and EPPO code are free text with no lookup.
claims.note: I looked at services/commodities/index.js, the details controller and template, and line-form.js. None of them offers a search or lookup of a commodity catalogue or of tariff, EPPO or species codes.

claims.statement: Seed potatoes have no origin narrowing: every country the origin block offers is acceptable, because reg 24A(1)(a) scopes them to the whole Common SPS Area.

A category the list never names — seed potatoes,
 * scoped by reg 24A(1)(a) to the whole Common SPS Area — narrows nothing, so
 * every country the origin block offers stays acceptable for it.

claims.statement: The origin constraints are ordered narrowest first. When a consignment breaks more than one, the origin page reports the narrowest.
claims.quote:
The order is the order the origin page reports a failure in: a consignment
 * that breaks more than one constraint is told about the narrowest.

claims.statement: The commodityType answer is a mandatory obligation.
The commodityLines obligation requires at least one line, with error code obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne. It is a structural group that is always in scope.
Each line's category is a mandatory obligation within commodityLines. It is the gate that every other per-line field reads.
claims.quote:
// The per-line gate. Every other field on a line reads it at the same identity
// level, so each gate is a same-frame `allowListed` with a null projection.

claims.statement: Each line's quantity is a mandatory obligation with no gate, because every line carries a quantity.
claims.quote:
// Every line carries a quantity, whichever category it is, so this one field
// needs no gate.

claims.statement: Genus, species, commodity code, variety, intended use, EPPO code, size of the trees and phytosanitary treatments are each mandatory obligations within commodityLines. Each applies only on lines whose category the commodity service lists for that field, with the reason code obligation.<field>.applicable.becauseCategory.
claims.quote:
applyTo: allowListed(
    category,
    () => categoriesRequiring(name),
    null,
    appliesBecauseCategory(name)
  )

claims.statement: The page that reveals a line's fields and the obligation that scopes them read the same category-to-field list, so the page asks exactly the fields the model requires.
claims.quote:
One list per field, read twice: the obligation's `applyTo` gate scopes the
 * field to these categories, and the entry page renders exactly the fields
 * whose list holds the chosen category.
